Get up and running.

Install once. Keep the controls you need close to your next attempt.

Install Wood

  1. Install and launch TUNG through Steam at least once.
  2. Download WoodSetup.exe. Close TUNG and Wood.
  3. Steam can stay open; setup does not change launch options.
  4. Run the installer. Confirm the detected TUNG folder, or use Browse to select it.
  5. Run setup to install Wood; your Steam and launch-wrapper settings are left unchanged.
  6. Click Install Wood, then launch TUNG normally.
  7. Press F10 or click Mods when the game is ready. Select Time Warp from the mod list to open its settings.
No separate Python or UE4SS download is needed. Setup includes the pinned runtime and native in-game menu.

Wood Utilities

Press F10 and select Wood Utilities to open its settings. Auto-speedrunner mode enables the game’s native speedrunner mode on startup; the separate music option controls its soundtrack. Turning auto mode off leaves your current run unchanged. Soundtrack selection applies on your next run, while switching music off also mutes it immediately.

One Application volume slider controls final audio output; set it to 0% to mute TUNG. One Sensitivity slider adjusts live mouse input from 0.10× to 3.00×. Reset sensitivity restores 1.00×; vanilla direction and smoothing are unchanged. Changes save automatically and survive updates.

Use Time Warp

Set a speed between 0.05× and 4× with the slider, presets, or exact speed field. Press Enter or Apply to save an exact value. Search by name or description and use All, Active, or Settings to filter the mod library. The in-game menu shows the speed confirmed by the engine.

KeyAction
F10Open or close the native mod menu
F6Halve world speed
F7Reset to 1×
F8Double world speed
EscapeReturn to the mod list, then close the menu

Disable Time Warp to restore 1× while retaining your selected speed. Reset speed on world change returns to normal speed when moving to another world. Settings persist between launches.

Use speed changes for practice or categories that permit tools. Check your category’s rules before recording a submitted run; Wood does not certify leaderboard eligibility.

Manage mods

The runtime scans the game’s Mods folder for standalone .lua mods and packaged .tungmod files. WoodSetup installs Time Warp and Wood Utilities there. Add a mod by placing its Lua file in that folder; disable it in the menu or remove the file to uninstall it.

Use the separate Wood Mod Packager to combine Lua source, metadata, and an optional PNG icon into a single .tungmod file. Packaged mod icons are shown in the in-game library when the image is supported.

Uninstall Wood

  1. Close TUNG and Wood before uninstalling.
  2. Open Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Wood for TUNG → Uninstall, or run WoodUninstall.exe in the TUNG folder.
  3. Click Uninstall Wood.

Uninstall restores owned files from backups and removes unchanged files installed by Wood. Personal settings, custom mods, and backups remain. Files you edited after installation are preserved and reported. Wood does not change Steam launch options.

Troubleshooting

Setup asks me to close TUNG.

Close TUNG and run setup again. Steam can remain open because setup does not modify Steam launch options.

TUNG was not detected.

Browse to the folder containing TUNG.exe and the TUNG subfolder. Install and launch the game through Steam once first.

F10 does not open the menu.

Wait for the world to initialize. Check TUNG/Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/UE4SS.log and .wood/status.json. Close the game and rerun setup if runtime files are missing.

The menu does not open.

Wait for the world to initialize. Check TUNG/Binaries/Win64/ue4ss/UE4SS.log and .wood/status.json. Close the game and rerun setup if runtime files are missing.

I already use another loader.

Setup stops if an incompatible dwmapi.dll proxy is present. Existing UE4SS installations and unrelated mods are preserved.
